description: An operating-system package on the scanned host that matched a vulnerable version range. Host findings are read-only for the agent (plan/00-SPINE.md S7, remediable_by_agent=false) but still need a stable identity so they can be tracked, suppressed, and reported as resolved.

mutations.name: version_bumped
mutations.description: A Debian point release. The version lives only in the purl and is stripped before hashing.

mutations.name: purl_carrying_an_arch_qualifier
mutations.description: Qualifiers are stripped with the version.

mutations.name: package_manager_uppercased
mutations.description: 'APT' and 'apt' are the same manager. The manager segment of the locator is lowercased, because a case difference between two scanner versions would otherwise fork every host finding at once.

mutations.name: package_manager_and_identifier_padded
mutations.description: Surrounding whitespace from a parsed CLI table is trimmed.

mutations.name: purl_already_version_free
mutations.description: PurlBase is idempotent, so a producer that already stripped the version agrees with one that did not.

notes: The host tier shares the SCA formula, parameterised by detector_kind. Its locator is '<package_manager>:<host_identifier>'.
host_identifier keeps its architecture suffix verbatim: 'openssl:amd64' and 'openssl:i386' are two installed packages the manager treats separately, so they are two findings.

The locator therefore contains more than one ':'. That is fine - it is a composed field, not a parsed one - but package_manager itself is rejected if it contains ':', because that would make the composition ambiguous.
